title: Accounting Mastery and the Close
subtitle: Chart of accounts, journals, reconciliation and a month-end you can finish on day three
outcomes: Design a chart of accounts that reports without Excel
Post the six journal patterns every business needs
Reconcile bank, receivables and payables monthly
Close a period with evidence, not optimism

slides.title: Chart of accounts: fewer accounts, more dimensions
bullets: Group accounts hold no postings; only ledger accounts receive journal entries
Account type drives behaviour: Bank and Cash reconcile, Receivable/Payable attach to parties, Accumulated Depreciation behaves differently on the balance sheet
Root types (Asset, Liability, Equity, Income, Expense) are fixed by ERPNext and must not be re-purposed
Prefer one account plus an Accounting Dimension over fifty near-duplicate accounts
slides.notes: The most common chart of accounts mistake is encoding dimensions in account names: Travel – Sales – North, Travel – Service – South, and so on. That multiplies rows, breaks comparability and makes the P&L unreadable. Use cost centres, projects or a custom dimension instead, then let the report group by them. A good chart of accounts fits on one screen per root type.

callout.title: The three-question test
callout.text: Will anyone report on it separately this year? Is a statutory filing keyed to it? Does a bank statement line need to match it? If all three are no, use a dimension.

slides.title: Six journal patterns that cover almost everything
bullets: Accrual: expense now, invoice later — debit expense, credit accrued liabilities; reverse when the invoice arrives
Prepayment: debit prepaid asset, credit bank; amortise monthly to expense
Depreciation: debit depreciation expense, credit accumulated depreciation — never credit the asset
Write-off: debit bad debt expense, credit receivable with the party and reference intact
Intercompany: two mirrored entries through the intercompany journal, never one-sided
Payroll: one entry per pay run with salary expense, statutory payables and net pay to bank
slides.notes: Journals are not a workaround for missing documents; they are the language of period accounting. Keep a naming convention in the remark field — ACCRUAL-2026-03, PREPAY-INSURANCE-2026 — and reverse accruals with the reversal date set explicitly, so next month's close does not depend on memory. Every journal should be explainable in one sentence to an auditor.

slides.title: Payment terms, advances and post-dated cheques
bullets: Payment Terms generate schedules; a 2/10 net 30 term needs two rows with credit days and discount percentage
Advances are payments without allocation — visible in Payment Reconciliation until consumed
Post-dated cheques are recorded as a payment with a post-dated reference date, or tracked in a dedicated register account
Payment Reconciliation is the tool that settles many invoices against many payments at once
slides.notes: Cash application is where finance teams lose weeks. Decide the policy for overpayments, short payments and bank charges once, then encode it: deductions on the payment entry, advances left unallocated and consumed later, write-offs only with approval. Run Payment Reconciliation weekly so the unallocated bucket never accumulates.

slides.title: Bank reconciliation that closes in an hour
bullets: Create the Bank doctype per account, then import Bank Transactions from statement CSV or connect the feed
Bank Transaction Rules auto-match common narrations against party, account and reference
Match each statement line to a Payment Entry, a journal or an invoice; matched lines leave the unreconciled pool
The Bank Reconciliation Tool shows the statement balance against the ledger balance and exposes anything unmatched
slides.notes: Reconciliation is a matching exercise, not a data-entry exercise. If you spend more than an hour a week per account, the problem is upstream: payments are not allocated to invoices, or bank charges are posted as journals with no reference. Fix the source and reconciliation becomes a review rather than an investigation.

callout.title: Never match to a journal
callout.text: A journal entry with no party or reference reconciles the balance but destroys the audit trail. Match to the payment or create one.

slides.title: The month-end sequence
bullets: Cut off transactions: agree the last goods receipt, delivery and invoice date with operations
Post accruals, prepayment amortisation, depreciation and payroll for the period
Reconcile bank accounts, receivables and payables to their subledgers, then review the GR/IR and advance buckets
Run the trial balance, P&L and balance sheet; investigate every movement you cannot explain in one sentence
slides.notes: A close is a sequence with owners and evidence, not a heroic evening. Publish the calendar: day one cut-off, day two journals, day three reconciliation, day four review, day five sign-off. Each step produces a document or a report that someone signs. If a step keeps slipping, it is usually a missing automation, not a lazy person.

slides.title: Freezing the past
bullets: Accounting Period or Period Closing Voucher blocks postings into a closed period
Accounts Settings controls whether users may edit or cancel submitted accounting documents, and who may back-date
Restrict back-dated entries to a small group; a back-dated receipt silently reprices everything after it
Keep the audit trail: version history, submission and cancellation logs, and immutable logs for statutory documents
slides.notes: Closing a period is a promise that the numbers will not change. Enforce it technically, not socially. Set the period close inside the first week, restrict back-dating to the finance lead, and review the Activity Log monthly for cancelled invoices — a spike there is either a training gap or a control failure.

callout.title: Who can back-date?
callout.text: One named person. Everyone else asks that person, and every request is logged in the document's remarks.

slides.title: Reading the statements like an operator
bullets: P&L: compare periods and dimensions, not just totals; a flat total hides two segments moving in opposite directions
Balance sheet: check inventory against the stock ledger, receivables against AR ageing, and bank against statements
Cash flow: the Cash Flow Mapper decides which accounts are operating, investing and financing — maintain it
Financial Report Builder assembles custom statements from row templates when the standard ones do not fit
slides.notes: Statements are a reconciliation surface, not a presentation. The balance sheet is only trustworthy if its inventory, receivables, payables and bank lines agree with the reports that own those numbers. Put that cross-check in the close checklist; it catches more errors than any variance analysis.
paths: Accounts > Reports > Profit and Loss Statement

slides.title: SST filing and e-Invoice reconciliation
bullets: SST-02 is filed from output tax less input tax; make sure your SST accounts are separate from other taxes
Reconcile submitted e-Invoices to the sales ledger for the period: total, count, and any cancelled or rejected documents
LHDN cancellations must be mirrored in ERPNext — a cancelled e-Invoice with a live sales invoice is the worst of both worlds
Keep the submission log export with the period's working papers; it holds the document hash and LHDN's response
slides.notes: The filing is arithmetic; the audit trail is the work. Malaysian auditors increasingly ask for the e-Invoice submission evidence alongside the ledger, so export the submission log monthly and file it with the close. If the numbers differ, the difference is almost always a credit note that was issued in ERPNext but never submitted, or the reverse.

callout.title: One number, two places
callout.text: Sales ledger total for the period must equal submitted e-Invoice totals plus any documents still in error state. Reconcile before filing, not after.

lab.title: Close a month with evidence
steps: Import a bank statement CSV as Bank Transactions and create two matching rules for recurring narrations
Match every statement line to a payment, an invoice or a new payment entry; leave nothing unreconciled
Post an accrual journal for an unbilled utility, set a reversal date in the next period, and verify the reversal appears
Post depreciation for one asset category and confirm the accumulated depreciation account increased while the asset stayed put
Run Trial Balance, P&L by cost centre and Balance Sheet; tie inventory to the stock ledger and receivables to AR ageing
Create a Period Closing Voucher for the month and attempt to post a back-dated journal — observe the block
Export the e-Invoice submission log for the month and reconcile its total to the sales ledger
lab.done: You can hand someone the close pack — reconciliation evidence, journals with reversals, and three statements that agree with their subledgers — and they can follow it without asking you a question.

quiz.question: Where does depreciation of an asset go?
options: Debit depreciation expense, credit accumulated depreciation
quiz.why: Accumulated depreciation is a contra-asset so the asset keeps its cost on the balance sheet while its carrying value falls.

quiz.question: A customer underpays by RM30 because of a bank charge. What is the cleanest treatment?
options: Amend the invoice to RM30 less
Post the payment with a RM30 deduction to bank charges
Write it off as bad debt
quiz.why: Deductions settle the invoice fully and book the fee to its own account, keeping both the receivable and the expense correct.

quiz.question: What does a Period Closing Voucher do?
options: Closes the fiscal year and resets balances
Blocks postings into the closed period
quiz.why: It prevents back-dated postings into a closed period; profit transfer happens through the year-end closing entry.

quiz.question: Which reconciliation should you run before trusting the balance sheet inventory line?
options: Inventory account balance against the stock ledger value
quiz.why: The balance sheet reads the GL; the stock ledger is the operational truth. Comparing them is the check that both received entries.

quiz.question: For a Malaysian period filing, what must be reconciled alongside the sales ledger?
options: Submitted e-Invoice totals, including cancelled and rejected documents
quiz.why: The ledger and LHDN's accepted documents must agree; unreconciled credit notes are the usual cause of a difference.

narration: Chapter six is accounting, and the theme is evidence. Start with the chart of accounts and with restraint. Group accounts hold no postings. Account type drives behaviour: bank accounts reconcile, receivables attach to customers, accumulated depreciation is a contra asset. The classic mistake is encoding dimensions in account names, which multiplies rows and destroys comparability; use cost centres or an accounting dimension instead. Then the six journal patterns: accruals with a reversal date, prepayments amortised monthly, depreciation against accumulated depreciation, bad debt write-offs that keep the party and reference, mirrored intercompany entries, and one payroll journal per run. Journals are the language of period accounting, not a workaround for missing documents, so name them consistently. For cash, the discipline is allocation: a payment not allocated to an invoice is not a settled invoice. Put bank charges on the payment as deductions, and never reconcile a bank line against a journal with no party, because it balances the account and destroys the trail. The close is a sequence with owners and dates: cut off transactions, post accruals and depreciation, reconcile bank, receivables and payables, then review the statements. Freeze the past with a period closing voucher and restrict back-dating to one named person. For Malaysia, reconcile submitted e-invoices to the sales ledger before filing SST-02.
